changes.summary: Homepage standings now put every team in this season's Premier League or D-League, matching the standings page.
The opponent matchup rank on Set Lineup and Rosters now averages over games played, so a defense coming off its bye no longer looks tougher than it is.
Ask Buck right on the History page: he shows what he's looking up, types his answer live, and follow-ups read as one chat you can share whole.
changes.headline: Buck answers live
changes.lede: Ask the History is a real conversation now. Type a question on The League's History page and Buck answers right there, showing each lookup as he runs it and writing his answer as you watch. Follow-ups pick up where he left off, and sharing sends the whole chat, first question included.

changes.summary: Buck's charts now show the same games his answer names, in the same order, instead of a different ranking.
Sharing a Buck answer to the group chat now posts a link to the whole conversation on the site, instead of a picture with no link.
Doc Rivers no longer tells managers to adjust lineups when a player is ruled out after his game has kicked off; the post reports it as in-game news.
Buck knows the AFL's American League and National League conferences, so "best NL team" questions get a real answer.
Full-screen ads no longer pop up between pages on our MFL league pages; your tap goes straight to the page you picked.
Standings switch to the new season on your league's own start date, showing 0-0 until Week 1, instead of waiting for Labor Day.
Christmas Week has a new evergreen and gold look, and it now works in both light and dark mode.

Banner and sticky-footer ads are gone from our MFL league pages, with no empty gaps left behind.
Every Thursday Schefter posts one waiver-wire list per league: each waiver claim, then the first-come-first-served pickups made after waivers ran.
